title: Power Falls Furthest
endLine: Fatigue lowers force and often speed, so power suffers most.

scenes.tts: Last time, power peaked at a middle load, about a third of the force the muscle can hold. Now make it lift that load again and again. Its holding force dips a little. Why can its power drop so much further?
scenes.narration: Last time, power peaked at a middle load, about a third of the force the muscle can hold. Now make it lift that load again and again. Its holding force dips a little. Why can its power drop so much further?
scenes.caption: Last time, power peaked at a middle load, about a third of the force the muscle can hold. Now make it lift that load again and again. Its holding force dips a little. Why can its power drop so much further?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: muscle BLUE (rounded block hanging from a GREY ceiling bar); load and force ORANGE; shortening speed YELLOW; external power GREEN; zero or rejected RED; question text and title GOLD; axes GREY. New in this film: calcium CYAN, inorganic phosphate MAGENTA, protons WHITE. A small tag 'model muscle, made-up numbers' sits at bottom right for the whole film. Opening layout: the BLUE muscle with an ORANGE load block below it fills the LEFT 40% of the frame and about 70% of its height. At RIGHT, two tall vertical bars on one baseline: ORANGE 'holding force' (scale 0 to 100 N, starts full at 100) and GREEN 'peak power' (scale 0 to 4 W, starts at 3.8). Recap on the first sentence: a faint ghost of the first film's GREEN power-versus-load hump flashes behind the bars with its peak marked near a third of the load axis, then fades. On 'again and again', the muscle lifts the load and lowers it in a steady rhythm; each lift is a little slower (schematic timing), and a small counter 'lifts' ticks up. On 'dips a little', the ORANGE bar sinks smoothly from 100 to 80. During the question, the GREEN bar sinks from 3.8 to 1.8 (the film's final model values), far more than the ORANGE bar. GOLD text across the top: 'Why does power fall further?'

Title 'Power Falls Furthest' fades in at top in GOLD for 2 s while the question text fades out. The muscle keeps lifting slowly in the background; the two bars reset to fresh values (ORANGE 100, GREEN 3.8).

scenes.tts: Fatigue is a fall in force or power during repeated activity that recovers with rest. It usually lowers the ceiling, its holding force. It often lowers the top speed too. And in most studies, the speed curve sags more.
scenes.narration: Fatigue is a fall in force or power during repeated activity that recovers with rest. It usually lowers the ceiling, its holding force. It often lowers the top speed too. And in most studies, the speed curve sags more.
scenes.caption: Fatigue is a fall in force or power during repeated activity that recovers with rest. It usually lowers the ceiling, its holding force. It often lowers the top speed too. And in most studies, the speed curve sags more.
scenes.visual: The two bars fold away; the muscle and load shrink to a small icon at top centre that keeps lifting slowly. The first film's two plots slide in and fill the frame below it, side by side, same axes as before. LEFT plot: speed v (m/s), 0 to 0.42, against load F (N), 0 to 105. RIGHT plot: power P (W), 0 to 4.2, against the same load axis. Fresh model curves, computed from v = b (F0 - F) / (F + a) with F0 = 100 N, a = 25 N, b = 0.100 m/s (top speed 0.40 m/s): YELLOW sagging speed curve on the left, GREEN power hump P = F x v on the right, peak 3.82 W at 30.9 N. On 'recovers with rest', a short GOLD tag 'recovers with rest' appears by the icon. Three GOLD handles appear on the speed plot as the narrator names them: 'ceiling' on the ORANGE end point at 100 N (it bobs down a little and back), 'top speed' on the YELLOW end point at 0.40 m/s (bobs down and back), and 'sag' on the middle of the curve (the curve bows a little lower and back). Schematic wiggles only; no values change yet.

scenes.tts: In the made-up model muscle, peak power starts near three point eight watts. Cut the ceiling by twenty percent, from one hundred newtons to eighty. Peak power falls by the same twenty percent.
scenes.narration: In the made-up model muscle, peak power starts near 3.8 watts. Cut the ceiling by 20 percent, from 100 newtons to 80. Peak power falls by the same 20 percent.
scenes.caption: In the made-up model muscle, peak power starts near 3.8 watts. Cut the ceiling by 20 percent, from 100 newtons to 80. Peak power falls by the same 20 percent.
scenes.visual: On 'three point eight watts', the GREEN peak dot glows with the label '3.8 W'. The fresh YELLOW and GREEN curves leave faint ghost copies labelled 'fresh', which stay for the rest of the film. On 'Cut the ceiling', the ORANGE end point of the speed curve slides left from 100 N to 80 N and the YELLOW curve reshapes live (F0 = 80 N, a = 20 N, b = 0.100 m/s, top speed still 0.40 m/s); the GREEN hump shrinks with it (peak 3.06 W at 24.7 N). Small ORANGE tag on the speed plot: 'ceiling -20%'. On 'the same twenty percent', the GREEN peak dot slides to the new peak, labelled '3.1 W', and a GREEN tag '-20%' appears beside it.

scenes.tts: Now let the top speed fall by twenty percent as well. That makes two cuts of twenty percent each. Does peak power now fall by forty percent?
scenes.narration: Now let the top speed fall by 20 percent as well. That makes two cuts of 20 percent each. Does peak power now fall by 40 percent?
scenes.caption: Now let the top speed fall by 20 percent as well. That makes two cuts of 20 percent each. Does peak power now fall by 40 percent?
scenes.visual: On 'top speed fall', the YELLOW end point on the speed axis slides down from 0.40 to 0.32 m/s with a YELLOW tag 'top speed -20%'; the YELLOW curve reshapes (F0 = 80 N, a = 20 N, b = 0.080 m/s). The GREEN power hump does NOT update yet: it stays at the 3.1 W shape, greyed slightly, as if waiting. On 'two cuts', the ORANGE '-20%' and YELLOW '-20%' tags pulse side by side. GOLD question card across the top: 'Power down 40%?'
Predict pause. The GOLD card 'Power down 40%?' stays. The small muscle icon keeps lifting slowly; the greyed GREEN hump shimmers faintly. No other change.

scenes.tts: Not quite. Power is force times speed, so the two cuts multiply. Point eight times point eight is point six four. Peak power falls thirty-six percent, to about two point four watts.
scenes.narration: Not quite. Power is force times speed, so the two cuts multiply. 0.8 times 0.8 is 0.64. Peak power falls 36 percent, to about 2.4 watts.
scenes.caption: Not quite. Power is force times speed, so the two cuts multiply. 0.8 times 0.8 is 0.64. Peak power falls 36 percent, to about 2.4 watts.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. On 'force times speed', the ORANGE and YELLOW tags fly toward each other and lock into one line between the plots: '0.8 x 0.8 = 0.64'. On 'falls thirty-six percent', the GREEN hump regains full colour and shrinks to its computed shape (peak 2.44 W at 24.7 N); the GREEN peak dot slides down, labelled '2.4 W', with a GREEN tag '-36%'. The 'fresh' ghosts stay visible above it.

scenes.tts: Now let the speed curve sag more, as it does in most studies. In this example, peak power falls about fifty-three percent in all, to about one point eight watts.
scenes.narration: Now let the speed curve sag more, as it does in most studies. In this example, peak power falls about 53 percent in all, to about 1.8 watts.
scenes.caption: Now let the speed curve sag more, as it does in most studies. In this example, peak power falls about 53 percent in all, to about 1.8 watts.
scenes.visual: On 'sag more', the YELLOW curve bows lower in the middle while both end points stay put (F0 = 80 N, top speed 0.32 m/s; a/F0 falls from 0.25 to 0.15, so a = 12 N, b = 0.048 m/s); YELLOW tag 'more sag'. The GREEN hump shrinks again to its computed shape (peak 1.80 W at 21.2 N); peak dot labelled '1.8 W', GREEN tag '-53%'. On 'fifty-three percent in all', the ORANGE end point at 80 N and its '-20%' tag glow, and a vertical bracket on the power plot from the fresh ghost peak (3.8 W) down to the new peak (1.8 W) glows GREEN.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. Fatigue lowers the ceiling, and often the top speed and the curve's shape too. Power depends on all of them at once, so it can fall further than force.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. Fatigue lowers the ceiling, and often the top speed and the curve's shape too. Power depends on all of them at once, so it can fall further than force.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. Fatigue lowers the ceiling, and often the top speed and the curve's shape too. Power depends on all of them at once, so it can fall further than force.
scenes.visual: The two plots slide apart slightly; between them, the two tall bars from the opening return side by side: ORANGE 'holding force' at 80 of 100 and GREEN 'peak power' at 1.8 of 3.8, each with its fresh level as a faint outline. On 'the ceiling', 'top speed' and 'shape', the three GOLD handles on the speed plot light in turn. On 'all of them at once', three thin lines run from the handles into the GREEN bar. On 'further than force', the gap between the two bars' drops glows. GOLD label under the bars: 'power pays for each loss'.

scenes.tts: So what pulls these down? The popular story blames lactic acid, but the evidence points away from the lactate ion. Leading suspects are inorganic phosphate and failing calcium release. Protons count too, to a smaller degree near body temperature. Their shares are still debated.
scenes.narration: So what pulls these down? The popular story blames lactic acid, but the evidence points away from the lactate ion. Leading suspects are inorganic phosphate and failing calcium release. Protons count too, to a smaller degree near body temperature. Their shares are still debated.
scenes.caption: So what pulls these down? The popular story blames lactic acid, but the evidence points away from the lactate ion. Leading suspects are inorganic phosphate and failing calcium release. Protons count too, to a smaller degree near body temperature. Their shares are still debated.
scenes.visual: Camera dives into the small BLUE muscle icon; plots and bars shrink to a small inset at top left (still showing the shrunken GREEN hump). Inside the fibre, schematic and filling about 65% of the frame height: a pale GREY thick filament with simple BLUE lollipop-shaped heads (labelled blocks, no molecular structure) beside a thin GREY actin rod, and a pale CYAN sac above labelled 'calcium store'. On 'lactic acid', a GREY token labelled 'lactate' floats in, then a RED cross stamps over it and it drifts aside, dimmed. On 'inorganic phosphate', MAGENTA tokens labelled 'Pi' gather around the heads. On 'failing calcium release', the CYAN calcium dots streaming from the sac thin to a trickle. On 'Protons', a few WHITE tokens labelled 'H+' appear, fewer and fainter than the Pi tokens; tag 'smaller near body temperature'. On 'still debated', three small GOLD question marks hover over Pi, calcium and H+; none is chosen.

scenes.tts: Do they act on the motor itself? In a laser trap, purified myosin heads pulled on one actin filament, with no lactate present. Acid cut their average peak force by about twenty percent. Phosphate, added at that low pH, largely abolished the strongest pulls. Myosin seemed to let go sooner.
scenes.narration: Do they act on the motor itself? In a laser trap, purified myosin heads pulled on one actin filament, with no lactate present. Acid cut their average peak force by about 20 percent. Phosphate, added at that low pH, largely abolished the strongest pulls. Myosin seemed to let go sooner.
scenes.caption: Do they act on the motor itself? In a laser trap, purified myosin heads pulled on one actin filament, with no lactate present. Acid cut their average peak force by about 20 percent. Phosphate, added at that low pH, largely abolished the strongest pulls. Myosin seemed to let go sooner.
scenes.visual: The fibre scene transforms: the calcium sac and the rest of the thick filament fade, leaving a small cluster of the same BLUE heads on a GREY platform below one actin rod. A pale beam cone from above holds a round bead tied to the end of the rod; tags 'laser trap' and 'no lactate' (the dimmed lactate token is gone). Each time a head grabs and pulls, the bead jumps sideways and an ORANGE force trace at right spikes (schematic trace, no units). On 'Acid', WHITE 'H+' tokens wash in and the ORANGE spikes shrink; a dashed line marks their average falling, tag 'about -20%'. On 'Phosphate', MAGENTA 'Pi' tokens join; the tallest spikes vanish, tag 'strongest pulls gone'. On 'let go sooner', each head's grip lasts visibly shorter and the spikes become narrow blips.

scenes.tts: In living rats, twitch force tracked phosphate more consistently than protons. That is an association, not proof of cause. How much each matters in working human muscle is still open.
scenes.narration: In living rats, twitch force tracked phosphate more consistently than protons. That is an association, not proof of cause. How much each matters in working human muscle is still open.
scenes.caption: In living rats, twitch force tracked phosphate more consistently than protons. That is an association, not proof of cause. How much each matters in working human muscle is still open.
scenes.visual: Pull back out of the trap to the fibre view, smaller, on the left. At right, three vertical meters side by side over a time strip (schematic, no numbers): ORANGE 'twitch force', MAGENTA 'phosphate', WHITE 'protons'. Over the strip, phosphate rises; force holds until phosphate passes a dashed MAGENTA mark labelled 'breakpoint', then falls in step with it. Protons rise smoothly too. A faint second strip below, tagged 'faster stimulation', repeats the same phosphate-force step, but the same proton rise now comes with a bigger force drop. On 'association, not proof', a GOLD tag 'association, not cause' sits across the meters. On 'still open', the three GOLD question marks from earlier return over Pi, calcium and H+ in the fibre.

scenes.tts: Back in the model, the tired muscle still held eighty percent of its force. Its power fell by more than half. Power is force times speed, so it pays for every loss at once.
scenes.narration: Back in the model, the tired muscle still held 80 percent of its force. Its power fell by more than half. Power is force times speed, so it pays for every loss at once.
scenes.caption: Back in the model, the tired muscle still held 80 percent of its force. Its power fell by more than half. Power is force times speed, so it pays for every loss at once.
scenes.visual: Pull all the way back to the opening layout: the BLUE muscle and ORANGE load at left, lifting slowly; the two tall bars at right with fresh outlines. On 'eighty percent', the ORANGE bar glows at 80 of 100. On 'more than half', the GREEN bar glows at 1.8 of 3.8. On 'force times speed', a slim YELLOW 'speed' bar (0.32 of 0.40 top speed) and a small YELLOW 'more sag' curve badge appear between the force and power bars and pulse; on 'every loss at once', force, speed and sag pulse together into the shrunken GREEN peak-power bar.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (the BLUE muscle slowly lifting its ORANGE load, the bars faint behind). Large white text, centred: 'Fatigue lowers force and often speed, so power suffers most.'
